Subject: POC model selection and trial plan - Acme Corp

Hi Samir + Lena,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great call. Quick recap and proposed next steps for the POC/trial so we can get alignment and schedule the work. I attached a short success criteria doc and a model performance matrix we discussed.

Recap / success criteria (high level):
- Latency: average 95th percentile < 600ms for interactive queries (targeting your EU region).
- Accuracy: at least 92% top-1 intent classification on your labeled test set (we'll run labels blind).
- Cost: token cost target under $0.006/1k tokens for steady-state traffic.
- Multilingual: support for EN, ES, PT with comparable accuracy to EN for core intents.
- Safety: no high-severity hallucinations on the 200-sample safety set.

Proposed evaluation plan / timeline:
1) Week 0 (this week): exchange sample datasets + agree on final success criteria doc (Marissa).
2) Week 1: Redwood sets up baseline models and ingestion pipeline; run initial evals (Aditya).
3) Week 2: Customer validation with your test harness; iterate on prompts and routing (Samir/Lena).
4) Week 3: Final run and decision for pilot expansion or adjustments.

Model selection (initial recommendation):
- Primary candidate: OpenLLama-13B (quantized 4-bit) — best balance of quality and cost for instruction-style chat + generation.
- Fallback: Mistral-7B (fast, lower-cost) for high-traffic degradation mode.
- Multilingual: evaluate Llama-based multilingual finetune or consider mT5/mT0 variant if EN performance drops on ES/PT.

Action items / owners:
- Marissa: finalize success criteria doc + share HubSpot deal link + timeline (today).
- Aditya: spin up model infra and run baseline evals (ETA 5 business days).
- Dev: prepare sample ingestion pipeline and temporary S3 link for samples.
- Samir/Lena: share sample dataset and list of key intents / edge cases.

Attachments: acme_poc_success_criteria.docx, model_performance_matrix.xlsx (stubs).

Please confirm the timeline and multilingual requirements so we can lock resources.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa — the recap looks great. A couple of clarifications from our side:

- Multilingual: Spanish (ES) and Portuguese (PT-BR) are must-haves for this pilot. We need parity on core intent detection for EN/ES/PT (within ~5% accuracy).
- Fallback behavior: in degraded mode we prefer shorter responses and more conservative generation (safety is important for our brand). How configurable is the fallback routing?
- Data: attaching a sample of 500 anonymized transcripts and a small labeled intent set (sample_data.zip) — will share via the Drive link you provided once access is set up.

On timing: a hard dependency for us is getting baseline results before the April 12 leadership sync. If you can meet the Week 2 run earlier, that would help.

On licensing: we need confirmation that the chosen open models' licenses are ok for commercial POC use — can Aditya weigh in?

Thanks,
Samir

Hi all — quick responses to Samir's questions + proposed evaluation specifics.

Licensing: OpenLLama and Mistral models are OK for commercial POC usage under their current licenses; we'll include a short license memo. If Acme legal needs more, we can escalate to our legal ops.

Model recommendations (concrete):
- Primary baseline: OpenLLaMA-13B-instruct (quantize to 4-bit using Redwood Optimize profile). Rationale: strong instruction-following, good quality/cost tradeoff.
- Fallback: Mistral-7B q4f16 (fast, smaller memory footprint). Configure routing policy to auto-failover on increased latency or token cost thresholds.
- Multilingual: run a parallel eval with a multilingual finetuned checkpoint (we have a recent internal mLlama-13B finetune) + mT0x for hard ES/PT cases. If EN->ES/PT gap >5%, we recommend targeted finetune on your labeled set.

Evaluation plan / metrics:
- Automatic metrics: intent accuracy, token-per-response, P95 latency, generation length, repeat/hallucination rate (heuristic).
- Human eval: 200-sample blind review across EN/ES/PT for safety and brand tone (1-5 scale).

Infra/setup ETA:
- I can spin up baseline containers + evaluation harness within 3 business days after we get sample data. We will run nightly evals and share a results sheet (model_performance_matrix.xlsx).

Dev notes for Dev Patel: please provision a temporary S3 bucket and grant read to aditya@redwood.com; Marissa will share access link. Also set up basic RBAC for the trial cluster.

Next steps: Marissa to share final success criteria (today). Samir to confirm Drive access + sample data. Aditya/Dev will target initial evals by end of next week.
